review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Some people think argue that advertising has good effect on economic. Many other hold a opinion, saying that this would cause negative social effect because it makes people unhappy with their life. In my opinion both of these views are correct.

On the one hand, advertising bring undeniable economic benefits. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand. When spending power is encouraged, production is encouraged, which create more employment opportunities and greater state revenue through taxation to contributing a stronger economy. For instance, e-commerce platforms like Shopee or Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers. This boosts not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector. Additionally, advertising creates jobs in marketing, media and design, which makes it an important driver of economic activity.

On the other hand, advertising has negative social consequences. Advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards or luxury possessions, which foster dissatisfaction among viewers. As an example, young people in particular feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook. This lead to frustration when they cannot afford them. In addition, advertising promote materialistic values and money-driven culture in the long run.
Overall, I think I agree at both views, it is valid to some certain extent, and advertising contribute to social dissatisfaction, also it play a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Some people argue that advertising has positive economic effects, whereas others believe that it can create social dissatisfaction. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand. Greater spending encourages production, creates employment opportunities and increases state revenue through taxation, thereby contributing to a stronger economy. For instance, Shopee and Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, which boosts both their sales and the wider digital retail sector. Furthermore, advertising creates direct jobs in marketing, media and design, making it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Constant images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards and luxury possessions may make viewers dissatisfied with their own lives. Young people can then feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or smart gadgets promoted on TikTok and Facebook. This pressure leads to frustration when they cannot afford such products. Over time, repeated exposure to these messages may encourage materialistic values and strengthen a money-driven culture.
In conclusion, advertising can stimulate economic activity and employment. At the same time, it may cause social dissatisfaction and strengthen a money-driven culture.

paragraphs: Some people argue that the news media have too much effect on people's lives and that this is not a positive development. Personally, I acknowledge this strong influence, although I am convinced that its effects are not entirely negative.

Admittedly, news media exert a considerable influence on people’s lives. One reason is widespread access to technological devices such as smartphones or laptops and to the Internet. These technologies allow people to follow the news instantly whenever and wherever they are; it naturally follows that the news becomes a regular part of their routine. Furthermore, the intense competition among news outlets means that, in order to gain attention, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content and present it in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and an eye-catching visual. That can reinforce the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that news media have both harmful and beneficial effects. Exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm people, making them feel anxious and helpless. Nevertheless, it is irrefutably true that when bad news is reported on varied social platforms, people are constantly warned of existing and coming problems in the society. A piece of news on a tragic accident, in which a family of four all lost their lives due to the father's driving under the influence of alcohol, can illustrate this warning role. If people are often exposed to this kind of news, they are much more likely to avoid drunk driving.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although news media have a considerable influence and can cause anxiety, they remain essential for public safety and awareness.

paragraphs: Some people assume that schools should reward students who show the best academic result, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements. From my perspective, both views have correct points, though recognizing progress brings different benefits.

On the one hand, admittedly rewarding students who show the best academic result is completely justified. First, students have diligently themselves to study of student, so they deserve their praise and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to gain the rewards, which can propel them towards overall academic gains. Second, this kind of competition can seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which can enable them to achieve success in later life.

On the other hand, however, students who show improvements should also be rewarded. Only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, which can cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. Consequently, they are prone to feeling overwhelmed and lost motivated, and gradually lose the incentive to study. By contrast, emphasizing improvements can encourage all student to diligent in their studies and assist students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves can even benefit students more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, while giving reward to top students is a natural practice, rewarding students who have improvements is also crucial to motivate every learner.

paragraphs: Some people assume that schools should reward students who show the best academic result, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements. From my perspective, both views have correct points, though recognizing progress brings different benefits.

Admittedly, rewarding students who show the best academic result is completely justified. First, students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, and thus they deserve their praise and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to gain the rewards, potentially improving overall academic results. Second, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. Students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which can enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who show improvements should also be rewarded. Initially, only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, which can cause others to think that their effort is futile. This is because they may feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals. Consequently, they are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, and gradually lose the incentive to study. By contrast, emphasizing improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students understand that they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves can even benefit students more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, while giving rewards to top students is a natural practice, rewarding students who show improvement is also crucial to motivate every learner.

paragraphs: In some nations, parents are opting to teach children themselves at home instead of sending them to school. Personally, I strong believes home schooling more disadvantage than studying at school.

On the one hand, some peoples who advocate homeschooling believe that allow parents to save money because no school fees are required. Children have home educated can less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both cause emotional and mental problems. Moreover, parents teaching their children at home by themselves can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, that often not case in traditional schooling because of the large class size.

On the other hand, this educational approach is not actually save financial for parents. Since parents need to pay a large amount of money to be cut off cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Besides that, most parents is not well for versed in all school subjects leading to difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. Moreover even social problems that children be faced with at school as bullying and having romantic feelings for others can become platforms supports they prepare for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, self-study at home for children with parent's supports is not actually bring more advantages than studying at school with teachers who have good knowledge in every different fields.

paragraphs: In some nations, parents are opting to teach their children at home instead of sending them to school. Personally, I strongly believe that homeschooling has more disadvantages than studying at school.

On the one hand, advocates of homeschooling point to several benefits. Initially, it allows parents to save money as no school fees are required. In addition, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, both of which can cause emotional and mental problems. Moreover, parents teaching their children at home can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones; this is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to large classes.

On the other hand, this approach has financial, academic and social drawbacks. Initially, it may not actually save parents money as they need to pay a large amount of money and spend time catering for their child's academic or personal needs. Besides that, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects, which can make it difficult to explain concepts properly and may cause academic problems. Moreover, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, studying at home with parental support brings some advantages, yet its financial, academic and social disadvantages outweigh them; studying at school with teachers who have knowledge in different fields is therefore preferable.
